name: Orison Synthform Loadout — Elongated Frame
description: Designed for synthetics with non-standard proportions — elongated limbs, narrow torsos, reversed-joint legs. A segmented bodysuit in smoke-grey adaptive mesh forms the base, with modular panel attachments that reconfigure via snap-tension rather than seams. Over it: a cropped asymmetric jacket with extended sleeve channels that accommodate limb length variance up to 40cm beyond human standard. Reversed-joint leg accommodation is built into the trouser via articulated gussets at the knee-analog joint. Footwear is a flat-soled wrap boot with adjustable tension strapping — no fixed heel. The silhouette is deliberately striking: this outfit doesn't pretend to be human-cut.
functionality: Snap-tension panels adjust to non-standard limb proportions without tailoring; articulated gussets accommodate reversed or multi-joint leg structures; extended sleeve channels for elongated arms; no fixed heel footwear for digitigrade or flat synthetic foot structures.
what_it_says: A synthetic who dresses for their own body, not an approximation of a human one.
worn_by: artists and performers with synthetic builds
story_hooks: Orison's founder disappeared during a Tier 5 corporate acquisition attempt — the label keeps running, no one knows who's making the decisions.
Wearing this in certain Tier 3 districts draws stares; wearing it in Tier 1 draws respect.
A specific colorway of this outfit is associated with a synthetic underground railroad moving artificial persons across corponation jurisdictions.
